title: Auth & multi-tenancy foundation
description: User, Role (lookup), Membership (polymorphic League/Team scope), Super Admin flag, JWT issuance/verification.

title: League/Team/Season domain model
description: League, Team, Season as first-class entities, plus TeamAffiliation (NHL/AHL/ECHL affiliate chain).

title: Player & roster history
description: Players as global identities (never a current-team FK), roster_spots for player+team+season so one player can hold rows on all three tiers in a year, and player_external_ids to reconcile sources that carry no NHL player id.

title: Game & stats domain model
description: Game, SkaterStatLine, GoalieStatLine as separate tables (not one combined wide table, per the prior attempt's lesson).

title: Backend skeleton & infra
description: rails new (API-only), Docker Compose (backend + db), health-check endpoint.

title: Frontend skeleton
description: Vite vs Next decided and scaffolded, Tailwind configured, auth screens wired to backend JWT.

title: Super Admin tools
description: Manual overrides: move a player between teams, edit records directly, bypassing normal scope checks.

title: External stats ingestion
description: Get real stat data into the system from the NHL's public web API (api-web.nhle.com). Throttled client called only from jobs; historical backfill by rake task, daily syncs via recurring.yml.

title: Role-based team operations
description: Write actions gated by Membership role, not read access — all views stay public. Coach: lineups (goalie, forward lines, defense pairings, scratches), hidden from other teams until they're historical. GM: call-ups/send-downs across a TeamAffiliation edge (parent team's GM only, not the affiliate's), trade proposals between teams, contract registration. Depends on TASK-3 for the underlying authorization check.

title: CBA salary cap compliance
description: Deferred, parked layer on top of EPIC-9's contract/trade actions: Averaged Club Salary and the Team Payroll Range (Article 50.5), the Bona-Fide Long-Term Injury/Illness Exception (50.10), and waiver-exemption tracking for send-downs (Article 13). Kept as its own epic rather than folded into TASK-39 so 'a GM can register a contract' shipping does not imply cap-legality is enforced. Researched against the source 2013 CBA on 2026-08-23 — see docs/DECISIONS.md.

title: Unified transaction log
description: A team-wide feed of trades, signings, waivers, and roster moves as peer transaction types (see e.g. PuckPedia's team transactions page), not just the roster_statuses history built for EPIC-3/EPIC-9. roster_statuses (IR/non-roster) is one narrow transaction type; trades and signings carry shaped data (multi-team assets, contract terms) that don't fit that table. Likely an event-log model that type-specific tables (trades, contracts, roster_statuses) feed into for one unified timeline, rather than generalizing roster_statuses itself. Depends on EPIC-9's trade proposal and contract registration actions existing first. Raised 2026-08-23, not yet scoped into tasks.

title: Admin data sync console
description: Superuser-only panel to trigger roster/stats/schedule/standings syncs on demand, scoped to a league, season, or single team, with live progress (e.g. '12/21 teams — syncing San Jose'). Sits on top of EPIC-8's existing sync services/clients rather than replacing them — one new AdminSyncOrchestratorJob loops through the resolved scope calling SyncTeamRoster/SyncStandings/etc. directly, tracked via new SyncRun/SyncRunItem rows (see DECISIONS.md, 2026-08-25). Shares the Super Admin surface with EPIC-7 but is a distinct concern: EPIC-7 is manual data overrides, this is operating the ingestion pipeline that already runs automatically via recurring.yml.

title: Advanced analytics schema: play-by-play, shifts, xG, rollups
description: Extends the existing domain model (League/Team/Season/Player/RosterEntry/Game/TeamStanding/SkaterStatLine/GoalieStatLine) with play-by-play events, shift data, versioned xG coefficients, and cached per-game/per-season advanced-stat rollups with a recalculation pipeline for corrected data. Backend only: schema, models, associations, indexes, and the recompute job structure. NHL API client calls for play-by-play/shift-chart ingestion are explicitly deferred to a later epic — these tables are built to accept upserts, not to be populated yet. A frontend to surface any of this is anticipated but not yet scoped as its own epic.

title: League-wide player search & stats table
description: A single searchable, filterable, sortable, paginated player list — backend-driven, not the client-side sort-only wiring DataTable has today. This is the actual trigger for TanStack Table's pagination/filtering row models, deliberately deferred until now (see docs/DECISIONS.md's DataTable entry: 'not built speculatively now'). Waited on EPIC-13 deliberately: sortable/filterable columns span both basic totals (skater_season_stats/goalie_season_stats) and advanced ones (Corsi/Fenwick/xG from player_season_advanced_stats), so this couldn't be scoped correctly before that data existed. Skaters and goalies stay separate views, not merged into one table — same reasoning already applied everywhere else in this schema (a combined skater+goalie shape was the prior attempt's mistake, per DECISIONS.md).

title: Play-by-play/shift ingestion; validate and surface advanced stats
description: Builds the ingestion path EPIC-13 deliberately deferred: a real NHL client for play-by-play and shift-chart data, upserting into game_events/shifts (TASK-58), wired through ComputeGameAdvancedStats (TASK-72) and the existing recompute pipeline (TASK-62) end to end — closing the composition point TASK-72 was left unwired at. Also validates the whole computation pipeline's accuracy against real data: on-ice attribution, Corsi/Fenwick/xG, and score-state splits (TASK-64) have only ever been exercised against synthetic spec fixtures, never a real game. Frontend: surfaces these now-real advanced stats, which requires building game detail and player detail pages that don't exist yet at all, plus extending the existing team stats page. TASK-81 broken out into its own epic (EPIC-23) once scoping made clear it was many tasks, not one — see EPIC-23. Every other task in this epic is done; epic complete.

title: Component library admin page
description: A super-admin-only page rendering every reusable presentational component from frontend/src/components (Text, Row, Stack, SegmentedControl, DataTable, Card, badges, etc.) with its variants/props side by side — a living style guide inside the app itself, not a separate Storybook.js build. Lets a dev sanity-check a shared component's look across every variant in one place instead of hunting through real pages, and doubles as a running check that TeamTheme/dashboard-redesign tokens stay consistent as new components are added.

title: Sync/ingestion efficiency
description: Redundant-work and reliability findings surfaced by actually running full historical NHL backfills against the real API for the first time, not by inspection — each confirmed against real dev data before being scoped. TASK-85 (done): whole-league per-game sync kinds were fanning out one item per team over the same shared game list, double-processing every game; restructured to run off the season's game list once. TASK-86 (done): RecomputeSeasonStats issued 14-19 separate aggregate queries per player instead of loading its rows once and summing in Ruby. TASK-88 (done): SyncGameStats recomputed a player's season stats once per game-stat row in a bulk sync instead of once per player, ~46x more calls than needed; now batched via RecomputeTouchedSeasonStats. TASK-89 (done): UpsertGameEvents/UpsertShifts re-queried Player/Team per row with no memoization, ~4,600 avoidable queries per game; now memoized per game. TASK-84 (done): dev had no persisted job queue, so an interrupted run couldn't resume, a retried run blindly redid finished work, and concurrent async jobs deadlocked each other on shared rows, plus GVL contention blocked the dashboard mid-sync; fixed via a real Solid Queue worker process (bin/jobs start --mode=async, avoiding a macOS-only fork crash found along the way) and idempotent resume in AdminSyncOrchestrator. TASK-90 (done): one flaky per-game request failed the whole run's status even when almost every game succeeded, and the activity log's fixed cap could hide the one line that explained why — fixed by recording every failed game on the item directly. TASK-91: the top-level status is still binary (any failure = failed), deliberately deferred as its own cross-stack change. TASK-93 (found live, once the real job queue was actually running): RebuildAdvancedStatsJob rebuilds a player's entire remaining-season advanced-stat chain per triggering game rather than just the new delta — with ingestion racing ahead of the single-threaded recompute consumer under real async load, this produced a 737-job, 12+ hour backlog blocking new sync runs from even starting. The theme has held all the way through: bulk/historical syncs were built by extending the daily-sync code path without accounting for how differently its costs, concurrency, and failure modes scale at full-season volume — and fixing the queue infrastructure (TASK-84) is precisely what made TASK-93 visible for the first time. TASK-91 (done): completed_with_errors distinguishes partial from total failure at both item and run level. TASK-94 (done): decoupled bulk ingestion from season-chain rebuild entirely. TASK-95 (done): RecomputeTeamSeasonAdvancedStats' own 11-queries-per-dimension bug, same shape as TASK-86. TASK-96 (done): a resumed run's progress counter had no reset point across a restart and could overcount past 100%. TASK-97 (done): CreateSyncRun's save-then-enqueue wasn't atomic. TASK-98 (done): sync_kinds dedup, batch-tracking-failure isolation, documented single-step cancellation gap. TASK-99 (done): five dead job classes removed. TASK-101 (done): GoalieGamePoints' own two-queries-instead-of-one. TASK-102 (done): goalie season-stat recompute batched the same way as game_stats'. TASK-103 (done): the whole advanced-stats pipeline's row-at-a-time writes replaced with a shared BulkUpsert (Ruby-side validation, one bulk statement), cutting a full per-game sync from ~2,600+ queries to ~120. TASK-104 (done): batch recompute steps gained per-row error isolation instead of one bad player/team crashing the whole run. TASK-100 (done): NhlClient/NhlStatsClient/HockeyTechClient's ~90% duplication extracted into a shared BaseApiClient. Epic complete. Reopened: TASK-105 found the decoupling TASK-94 introduced left a real gap for 2024-25 (fully ingested, season-rollup never separately triggered) — no follow-up task existed to close that loop. TASK-105 (done): individual/season-stat expansion (faceoffs, shots attempted/missed/blocked) plus a new self-service rebuild_season_stats sync kind, and a second real bug found/fixed along the way (dimension_start_games anchoring on preseason games instead of the right game_type) — both 2024-25 and 2025-26 now at 100% regular-season advanced-stat coverage. Epic complete.

title: Shot-location & danger-zone foundation
description:
Shared plumbing every other analytics/visualization epic below (EPIC-19 through EPIC-22) draws from, so a team heatmap, a skater zone map, and a goalie zone chart are three consumers of one thing, not three separate builds. Three decisions from planning are locked in here: danger-zone boundaries adopt an existing public standard (the “home plate” high-danger/mid-range/long-range shot-danger zone definition popularized by War-on-Ice and still used by Natural Stat Trick/MoneyPuck) rather than one invented for this app; any xG-colored visual is held back until TASK-81 replaces XgFormula's placeholder distance+angle coefficients with a trained model, so the shot-location/heatmap work here ships by raw shot count/rate, not xG weight; and Zone Time (the NHL Edge-style % of shift time in each zone) gets built for real rather than dropped in favor of the zone_entries/zone_exits counts already tracked on PlayerGameAdvancedStat — those answer a different question (controlled entries/exits, not time-in-zone) and don't substitute for it.

Everything here reuses geometry XgFormula already established: GameEvent.x_coord/y_coord normalized against target_net_x (resolved from home_team_defending_side, which flips by period), the same distance/angle calculation. Zone Time is the one genuinely new derivation: GameEvent.zone is per-event, not continuous, and Shift only has period/start_time_seconds/end_time_seconds with no zone-at-start field — so a team's zone occupancy has to be reconstructed by forward-filling each event's zone from its timestamp until the next zone-relevant event, then intersected with each shift's time window to get a per-shift zone split. That's new derived logic on top of data we already have, not a new NHL API call.

title: Team analytics page
description: Turns the team page from roster/schedule/stat-tables (TeamOverviewPage, TeamRosterPage, TeamSchedulePage, TeamStatsPage) into somewhere there's an actual read on the team: a top-players widget, a game-over-game trend, and the team shot heatmap from the original planning conversation. The trend data already exists and is currently invisible — TeamGameAdvancedStat has one row per game per team per strength/score-state split, sitting unused for anything but the single-game view on GamePage. Depends on EPIC-18 for the shot heatmap (rendered by raw shot count/rate, not xG, per that epic's decision) and reuses TeamStatsPage's existing strength_state/score_state segmented controls rather than inventing new filter UI.

title: Skater comparison tool
description: Player-vs-player comparison, NHL Edge-style, called out directly in planning. Scoped as N-way from the start (not a fixed 2-up), so the comparison route and layout need to actually hold up at 3+ players, not just visually degrade past two. Picker reuses LeagueSkaterSearch's existing search/sort (EPIC-14); per-player panels combine a shot-location zone map and Zone Time chart from EPIC-18 with rate stats already fully computed on SkaterSeasonStat/PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat. Zone Time specifically depends on EPIC-18's per-shift derivation landing first — without it this ships with zone maps and rate stats only, which is a reasonable partial slice if EPIC-18's zone-time tasks slip.

title: Goalie deep-dive & goalie comparison
description:
Danger-zone save%/shots-against splits and game-state splits for goalies, plus goalie-vs-goalie comparison (N-way, same as EPIC-20). The schema decision from planning: goalie advanced stats get a row-per-split shape matching PlayerGameAdvancedStat/TeamGameAdvancedStat (new GoalieGameAdvancedStat + GoalieSeasonAdvancedStat tables), not new named columns bolted onto GoalieGameStat the way even_strength_goals_against/power_play_*/shorthanded_* already are — consistent with how every other advanced-stat shape in this schema works, and the only one of the two options that has a clean place to hang score_state and danger-zone splits without multiplying columns per combination.

Carries the most open questions of the analytics work: GameEvent doesn't carry a goalie reference, so attributing a shot-against to the specific goalie in net (needed for any per-goalie split at all, danger-zone or otherwise) isn't obviously wired today and needs a recon spike before the rest of this epic can be scoped with confidence — see TASK-122. Depends on EPIC-18's DangerZone classifier for the zone buckets themselves.

title: Team-to-team comparison
description: The third leg of the comparison tools from planning, and the cheapest full slice of the four analytics epics — mostly assembly of what EPIC-18/EPIC-19 already build (TeamSeasonAdvancedStat, standings data, the team shot heatmap and game-over-game trend component) into an N-way side-by-side layout, rather than new schema or ingestion work. Worth shipping early, once EPIC-18 lands, to prove the N-way comparison pattern before it's reused by the heavier skater/goalie comparison epics.

title: Train and land a real xG model
description: TASK-81 (originally under EPIC-15) turned out to be many tasks once actually scoped — broken out here. Recon done 2026-08-30 (see project scoping doc): 4,420 games / ~375k Fenwick shot events / ~27k goals already ingested and validated (TASK-106's rake task), enough to fit against today, no new ingestion needed. The active XgModel is v0-placeholder, made-up coefficients, confirmed wrong live (TOR @ ANA 2026-03-30: 10.55-12.10 combined team xG against a realistic 2-4). Four decisions settled during scoping: velocity is dropped from the feature set entirely — NHL Edge (confirmed reachable, unauthenticated, same api-web.nhle.com host) only exposes season-level aggregates/top-10-hardest-shot per player, never a value for an arbitrary shot, so there's no path to a velocity column on every game_events row; training tooling is a one-off Python script (pandas + scikit-learn), the first Python in this repo, not a new service; the model family is logistic regression, matching XgModel.coefficients' existing weighted-sum-through-sigmoid shape exactly (a gradient-boosted model would need a real serving redesign and is a future option, not v1); and historical player_game_advanced_stats/team_game_advanced_stats get backfilled against the new model once it activates, riding TASK-62's existing recompute-chain machinery. Unblocks six backlog items explicitly held on this: TASK-109, TASK-115, TASK-123, TASK-129, TASK-134.

title: Draft pick inventory & lottery odds
description: Track B from claude/analytics-viz-roadmap.md (project docs), raised separately from the analytics/visualization push: pick tracking has to exist before trades can move picks, and lottery odds are wanted for the current season. No Draft/DraftPick model exists today (confirmed: no such migration/model in backend/app/models). EPIC-9 (in progress) is where trade-proposal actions live (TASK-38, backlog) and EPIC-11 (backlog, unscoped) is the unified transaction log that depends on EPIC-9's trade actions existing first — neither currently treats a pick as a tradeable asset. This epic covers the DraftPick model and lottery-odds display; making TASK-38's trade actions pick-aware is a task on EPIC-9 (see TASK-148), not part of this epic, per the roadmap doc's own call not to stand up a parallel trade system.

title: Full game boxscore (goal summary, penalties, period detail)
description: Track C from claude/analytics-viz-roadmap.md (project docs): GamePage today only shows player stat tables and whole-game advanced-stat totals (Api::V1::GamesController#show — skaters, goalies, advanced.players/teams, zone_time; confirmed reading it 2026-08-30). Recon: GameEvent already stores goal events fully attributed (primary_player=scorer, secondary/tertiary=assist1/assist2) and penalty events (primary_player=committed-by, secondary_player=drawn-by), with period/period_time_seconds/team/strength_state, via UpsertGameEvents — confirmed reading game_event.rb and upsert_game_events.rb. GoalieGameStat.decision/starter/saves/shots_against are already computed and already serialized by GoalieGameStatSerializer, just not rendered as a boxscore line. Genuinely missing: penalty infraction type/duration (no column on GameEvent, and the play-by-play payload isn't confirmed to carry it in a stored field); period-by-period score/shots-on-goal (no existing serializer path, though derivable from GameEvent). Open question, needs a live check before the penalty/period tasks are real: NhlClient#boxscore (already called by SyncGameStats) hits the same /v1/gamecenter/{id}/boxscore endpoint that publicly is known to carry a summary object (scoring/penalties/linescore/three-stars, per community references like the Zmalski docs already cited in claude/xg-model-scoping.md) — nothing in this codebase has read that part of the response yet, so it's unconfirmed whether goal/penalty/period detail is better sourced from the boxscore response already fetched than from deeper play-by-play parsing. See TASK-149.
